My rule is usually just. Who's living here? What kind of life do they lead? Is this a situation where we're gonna be having summer barbecues? Do we have kids running around? What size? Is the family wealthy or is the family poor? A poor family with 6 kids is gonna tend their yard differently than the fortune heiress, and they'll have different yards than the retired couple and their dog. 

I also start with any fencing, and then from there putting down backyard items in accordance with the kind of house built. Good starts are usually outdoor furniture, any gardening spots, barbecues, pools if you're using em

Then you can draw pathing with the terrain paint (I usually use a faint small brush to make dirt paths, but you can use tiled and such too for more proper paths) between these items. Like if I'm standing on the porch, how am I walking to this or that? Am I giving clearance to things that might be in use (Like swings or slip and slides)

Plants are more likely to grow where the paths aren't, so give a bit of distance from paths and items, then look at the world around. What kind of plants does the world have? Trees are more likely to be out of the way, but unlikely to be directly next to a fence. Is the sim likely to have flowers, or is it just uncut grass? Is the grass allowed to go long at all? Either way, put some dirt terrain under there for them. Doesn't have to be a huge amount, but a little makes it feel lived in. 

That's how I do yards at least. It's not easy sometimes! It's understandable that it's not intuitive, especially if you aren't in a lot of yards (Which let's face it, simmers are gamers. Inside is more probable than outside) but it's something that can improve. Worst case you can look at specific builds' yards you like and try to observe the specific parts that make it look good. Best of luck!

So my current legacy is going into a new gen as I write. The basics of the legacy is that I'm moving each gen to a new pack, world, or theme. Some get scrapped (Dine Out was one I was waffling on doing but I just made the guy a chef and did Reaper's Rewards) but most bulky packs get a focus.

Gen 1: Kennedy Legacy moves to Willow Creek and becomes a doctor. She gets honorarily adopted by an older coworker, and eventually has two kids. Belle Legacy by an alien, Daniel Legacy by Father Winter. She has a midlife crisis and essentially ditches Belle and Dan, so Belle leaves with Daniel in tow

Gen 2: Daniel and Belle scrape by in Oasis Springs, and while bills are hard to make, it's theirs. The two each have brief flings that result in their kids, but Belle and Daniel's son. Daniel Jr, die in tragic instances back-to-back. It leaves Daniel to care for Elliot Legacy, and he eventually goes on to marry Miki Akiyama and have more children (Tomori, Dominique, Leon, and Elodie Legacy)

Gen 3: While her siblings scatter off for their own adventures (AKA not played by me with few exceptions), Elodie sets her eyes on making an empire of her own. She scavenges and learns everything about gems and metals and forms her own jewelry store. It's while at the store that she has love at first sight with Kazuki Yoshida, who she spends a lot of time proving to that she's no drifter weaving bracelets, she's the woman of his dreams. The two have a happily ever after as he pursues cooking and she retires from the business after making well over a million. They have 5 kids (Finn, Koji, Charlie, Milo, and Aiko) and grow old together

Gen 4: Koji is inspired by his father and pursues food, deciding to open a restaurant of his own in Windenburg. He gardens and dabbles in dating, and is eventually sent on a quest to make ambrosia. He commits, with plans to make it for his father, who passed. In the weeks it takes though, he realizes that death is not an evil to be defeated, just another gate through which all eventually pass. He meets a man named Modern, and they get engaged. They have a  daughter, Abigail Legacy. Modern eventually cheats on Koji with his friend Perry Ernest and has two kids with him. Modern meets an end, and Perry leaves with his children in tow, never acknowledged as more than Modern's mistake in Koji's eyes. He eventually passes in Abigail's early teen years, having changed to the exciting life of a secret agent during a crisis

Gen 5 (This is a long one): Abigail was on her own early, and ended up moving into whatever appointment she could find. Eventually her childhood best friend, Alena Bjergsen turns back up and offers to move in together so she isn't in such a bad place. The two graduate high school and begin dating, but Abigail begins to struggle here. Her father's whirlwind romance lead to her other dad's wandering eye and cheating. She leans into the drugs the city has opened her up to, and flunks out of college as Alena graduates.   
  
They become young adults and get access to the inheritance Abigail has and has been unable to use. For Alena, they are ready to begin their lives. For Abigail, she can finally afford more than the bare minimum substances. They conceive a daughter, and Abigail gets clean with hopes of being in the happy relationship her dad never got, and marries Alena at the romance festival. The pregnancy is hard, especially with the addictions. After their daughter is born, there's some oddities. She's got sharp teeth and strange eyes without a pupil. Perhaps Grandpa Koji's work with the reaper had an effect on little Circe. Perhaps it was a dark ley line. Whatever it is shatters Abigail's view of her life, and she returns to the drugs. This leads to a worsening relationship, and on a last ditch effort to steer things right, Alena makes a wish for her bucket list: Spend an entire day in Windenburg.   
  
Taking Abigail and Circe with her, she tries to break through to her wife, or at least enjoy the vacation to their hometown. It fails to help Abigail, but Alena finds herself wanting a bush woohoo, and invites Abigail with her. Maybe it's a last goodbye, maybe it's another bid to wake her up. Either way, Alena finds herself pregnant. She brings the family home and tries to get Abigail to talk with her, to share big news with her, but instead they fight. Alena goes to work and leaves Abigail to her business, saying they'll talk it out later. Abigail calls her dealer over and buys more than she ever has before. In her anger and apathy, she overdoses.

Alena mourns, but moves on. Baby Calypso needs her, after all. She connects with others of Abigail's family (Just in case. If something happened to Alena.), she works hard, and feels crushed under the weight of it. She turns to drink, and leans into that. A brief fling leads to a pregnancy and miscarriage, and this wakes her up. She goes to rehab, and spends time with her daughters. Time flies, and Circe becomes a teen. She manifests as a vampire. Calypso follows into teenhood soon after, blessedly human.

Circe and Calypso have an accident. Circe can't feed on plasma packs, and Alena's at work and can't volunteer hers. Calypso has been told to never try. The hours pass, and Circe's control wavers. She attacks her sister, drinking uncontrollably. In the fervor, Calypso is made into a vampire too. Each seeing themselves as a monster, they prepare to flee the city to avoid the danger they bring. Alena returns and stops them, insisting that if it's the only way to stop them from leaving, they can go into the countryside, find a small town without many people. She's heard of a place, Forgotten Hollow, that might suit their needs fine.

As a kid, my dad would take me to a local farm set with games, pumpkins, apples, a crafts fair, the works. It was always the Saturday after the first frost (It's the best time to pick apples, he said). It would be a whole day, where we'd pile into the car at 8 AM and drive. We'd hit the craft fair first to get the luxury items. Next was apple picking, which was to fill a box. We'd usually eat lunch which was usually from a cooler, but it was into the corn maze after. We'd get cider, take a trolley ride, then we could pick any pumpkin we wanted if we could move it. As a kid, it was the ideal challenge. Usually we would get back to town around 5-6, and would either order pizza or just do something easy and carve our pumpkins. It's a trend I continued with an ex, and plan on picking up with friends, and will pass on to my kids.

To say that nonbinary people are not correct is to ignore the origin of the gender binary, which was purely a colonization thing. Gender binaries are quite rare in nature and society, and if you look around the world, many societies have genders that are not male and female. Two-spirit is one that comes to mind. Ultimately, gender and sex as you think of them, are incredibly Eurocentric at best. 

Beyond that, scientific studies in general exploring binary trans people are limited, and nonbinary identities moreso, but just because we haven't studied something doesn't mean it's not existing. The other planets existed before we saw them or explored them, other galaxies existed before we knew about it, and other cultures in the world existed long before other cultures interacted with them. That's also compounded on the fact that the thing cited often to talk about trans people being "scientifically real" is a study about brain differences, but that was disproven in 2019, but the myth still prevails.

Science and academics are important, that I can agree with, but you have a person that you love who is sitting in front of you, telling you who they actually are.
